title: spec(ai): a blueprint field cannot declare `multiple`, `accept` or `maxSize`, so an AI build of a multi-file or multi-record field is refused (cloud#4400)
body:
repo:cloud#2 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWTyRFQwYN1hZXbCHL

Filing category: ① product defect (AI build door), the blueprint half of the field contract.
reach: public entry `/api/v1/mcp` `apply_blueprint` (cloud). Measured by a test on the real build door at cloud main + cloud#4613, framework pin `b914e724`: a blueprint field `{ name: 'invoices', type: 'file', multiple: true }` is refused `blueprint_validation_failed`, `unrecognized_keys` at `objects.0.fields.2.multiple`, nothing staged. `accept` and `maxSize` are refused the same way.

## Business reason

"Expense claim with its e-invoices attached" is one sentence, and the natural model is one file field holding several invoices. A blueprint cannot say "several" (or which file types, or how large), so the AI builds a single-file field and then has to patch it with `update_metadata`.

## Where the gap is

`packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts`: `BlueprintFieldSchema` (lenient) and `StrictField` (the strict mirror the in-app design model generates against) declare `name, label, type, required, reference, options, summaryOperations, expression, defaultValue`. `FieldSchema` (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`) already declares all three keys:

- `multiple`: declarable only on `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` ∪ `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` (select, radio, lookup, user, file, image; redundantly multiselect, checkboxes, tags), and `radio` + `multiple` is refused. The refusal is the superRefine that uses `multiDeclarableTypeSet()`.
- `accept`: `z.array(z.string())`, MIME types or extensions, for the media family.
- `maxSize`: `z.number().int().positive()`, bytes, for the media family.

cloud cannot carry the keys on its own: `apply_blueprint` refuses every key `BlueprintFieldSchema.shape` lacks (cloud#3619), and the applier copies an allow-list of the parsed field. Accepting them in cloud alone would be a second, cloud-only dialect of the blueprint contract, and the in-app design path (strict mirror) still could not emit them.

## Expected

- `BlueprintFieldSchema` and `StrictField` declare `multiple`, `accept` and `maxSize` with `FieldSchema`'s own value shapes (strict side: `.nullable()`), each describe naming where it applies.
- The blueprint field's refinement refuses `multiple: true` on a type outside the declarable set by name at `['multiple']`, using the same set function as `FieldSchema` (no second copy of the type list). Whether `accept` / `maxSize` outside the media family are refused or left as on `FieldSchema` follows `FieldSchema` (today: not refused).
- The key-parity and VALUE-parity pins in `solution-blueprint.test.ts` cover the three keys.
- Precedent: `defaultValue` came onto the blueprint field the same way (objectstack#30584, ruling B on cloud#3619).

## After it lands (cloud#4400, not this card)

cloud's undeclared-key refusal admits the keys with no edit (it reads the schema's shape). cloud#4400 then carries them into the built field in `objectBodyWithSharing`, names them in the `apply_blueprint` description and the blueprint guide, re-reads the build-prompt baseline (the strict mirror grows), and tests the claim/invoices build end to end. cloud#4400 carries `Blocked-by:` this card, then the pin bump that brings it.

Metadata-protocol: widened (three keys the field contract already declares, added to the blueprint field and its strict mirror).
Clause-②: yes (widening) — a blueprint field carrying `multiple` on a multi-capable type, or `accept` / `maxSize`, parses where it is refused today.
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue BlueprintFieldSchema multiple` → 1 hit (#20827, unrelated); `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue blueprint field multiple` → 8 hits, none on this.

Reader who acts: the lane that owns `packages/spec` (`spec/ai`). Blocks: objectstack-ai/cloud#4400 (p2).
